findings.title: slice(1, limit + 1) drops the newest invoice on every page
findings.explanation: The page should be `rows.slice(0, limit)`. Starting at index 1 skips the first row, which is the newest invoice on the first page and the first row after the cursor on later pages. Each page also returns only `limit - 1` rows when more data exists. Rows are silently lost, and `next_before` still points at the last returned row. Change it to `rows.slice(0, limit)`.

findings.title: Possible crash on an empty result
findings.explanation: With `slice(1, ...)`, a result of exactly one row gives an empty `page`. That is harmless while `hasMore` is false. The slice offset is wrong, though, so `page[page.length - 1]` depends on a mistaken assumption. Fixing the slice to `slice(0, limit)` removes the risk, because `hasMore` then guarantees `page` is non-empty.

findings.title: No tests for pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: The bug above would have been caught by a test. Add tests for these cases: fewer than `limit` rows, exactly `limit` rows (`next_before` is null), `limit + 1` rows (`next_before` is set and the next page returns the remaining row), and no rows. Also check that walking all pages returns every invoice exactly once.

findings.title: Name the page-size arithmetic
findings.explanation: Use a named value such as `const fetchSize = limit + 1` and a short comment, so it is clear why one extra row is fetched. Tenant isolation is preserved: `org_id` is still filtered, and the query is parameterized.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
